wins.text: Services revenue up 8% YoY with fees up 10%; TTS cross-border volumes up 9%, commercial card spend up 5%; Securities Services AUC/A up 11%; segment ROTCE of 24.1%
Investment Banking revenue grew 35% and overall Banking revenue grew 49% YoY, driven by near-record investment-grade DCM issuance and ECM pickup in convertibles
Organizational simplification complete: ~7,000 positions eliminated generating $1.5B annualized run-rate expense saves, with $2.0B–$2.5B cumulative saves targeted in medium term
CET1 ratio ticked up to preliminary 13.5%, approximately 120 bps (~$13B) above regulatory minimum of 12.3%; tangible book value per share grew to $86.67

U.S. Personal Banking revenue up 10% YoY; branded cards interest-earning balances up 10%; retail services revenues up 18%; USPB delivered sixth consecutive quarter of double-digit revenue growth in retail banking

risks.text: USPB cost of credit rose 34% YoY to ~$2.2B driven by NCLs of $1.9B; Retail Services NCL rate of 6.32% came in above the high end of full-year guidance range and expected to remain above range in Q2
Wealth revenues declined 4% YoY with NII down 13% from lower deposit spreads and higher mortgage funding costs; ROTCE of only 4.6% well below medium-term target of 15%–20%

Transformation execution risk: management acknowledged intensifying efforts in automating regulatory processes and data related to regulatory reporting, signaling areas of lagging progress on consent order
Markets revenues down 7% YoY as lower volatility weighed on rates and currencies (down 21%); fixed income revenues declined 10%

Card late fee regulatory rule being implemented earlier than assumed, with potential NII headwind embedded in $80B–$81B guidance; persistent inflation and higher rates pressuring lower-FICO card customers

guidance_items.detail: Full-year 2024 revenue guidance of $80B–$81B unchanged, with NII ex-Markets expected down modestly and growth driven by noninterest revenue
Full-year expense guidance of $53.5B–$53.8B (ex-FDIC special assessment) reaffirmed; quarterly expense trend expected to decline from Q1 levels through year-end
Retail Services NCL rate now expected closer to high end of full-year guidance range; branded cards NCL rate in line with expectations and within guided range
Medium-term ROTCE target of 11%–12% reaffirmed; medium-term expense range of $51B–$53B unchanged

analyst_concerns_not_in_prepared: Mexico Banamex IPO timeline and whether a private sale could be back on the table given upcoming election and potential new administration
DFAST/stress capital buffer (SCB) volatility given transformation-depressed earnings and repositioning charges
Specific dollar quantum of card late fee revenue and earlier-than-expected regulatory implementation impact on NII
